access_differences.http: All three use the same OData HTTP endpoint, 51 requests and 1074741 response body bytes; fresh HTTP client per scan.
access_differences.cds: ABAP uses internal Open SQL against CDS (50 nonempty packages); external clients use SAP ABAP ODBC over verified HTTPS (51 logical fetch attempts).
access_differences.native: ABAP uses its existing primary HANA ADBC connection; external clients use a separate read-only HANA principal. All use 51 logical fetch attempts.
access_differences.resource_limits: The 1 CPU/256 MiB limits apply to external clients. ABAP runs inside the shared SAP container and is not isolated to these limits.
access_differences.sql_connection_lifecycle: Persistent block connection, new cursor per scan. First connection is in warmup; final session teardown is outside the measured window.
access_differences.deadlines: External requests and ABAP HTTP use 10 seconds; every scan uses 120 seconds. ABAP CDS/ADBC cannot enforce the same per-call cancellation as external drivers.
access_differences.byte_metrics: SQL body_bytes=0 means no HTTP application response body metric, not zero network traffic.
